[hermit2, degraded-unresolved, gpt-5.6-sol, devbig014, role=impl]

## Plain Language Summary

Teach the Reverie KVM backend to handle Linux syncfs calls. Ordinary guest files reach the matching host filesystem operation, while synthetic proc files and captured output keep their guest-visible filesystem identity instead of flushing private carrier storage.

## Project Impact

This closes one KVM syscall gap needed by Hermit backend parity. The change is stacked on repaired https://github.com/rrnewton/reverie/pull/610 at ae36d9aba36bc7f23cda33bb9889920d20d6feea because it relies on authenticated synthetic-proc descriptor identities. It does not yet change the Hermit pin or parity manifest.

## Determinism

The operation remains synchronous while the selected guest runs, matching current Detcore PassThrough ordering. Background execution would be unsound without a modeled filesystem-wide barrier because syncfs covers an entire superblock. Host writeback errors remain external inputs, so this change does not claim host-independent record/replay or L2 log parity.

## Linux Semantics

The handler consumes the low 32-bit signed fd value, returns EBADF for closed and O_PATH descriptors, invokes host syncfs exactly once for ordinary descriptors, and preserves exact host errno values including EIO, ENOSPC, and EDQUOT. Pipes and Unix sockets follow native Linux success behavior. Authenticated synthetic proc descriptors, loginuid, and capture-mode output pipes succeed without flushing their physical carriers. Synthetic fdinfo deliberately remains ENOSYS.

## Validation

At exact head 25306805dd5aefa1c73d844a48649c7266d951d3: formatting and strict all-target Clippy passed; 4 of 4 focused syncfs tests passed; the inherited long-path recvmsg/recvmmsg regression passed; the exact fdinfo test passed; 856 of 856 serial library tests passed; and the required real-KVM static ELF test passed 1 of 1. All nine reversible syncfs mutations were refreshed at this exact head and each was rejected by the intended assertion. The real-KVM result is output, exit-status, and repeat-parity evidence only; it is not L2 log parity.

## Relationship to gVisor

No gVisor code is copied. Linux behavior was checked against native kernel probes; the implementation stays in Reverie KVM descriptor translation and authentication paths.

## Human Review Required

Post-facto review trigger 1 applies because this adds syscall support. Independent exact-head Codex and actual Claude-family reviews are required before ready-for-review or merge. Source sites are marked TODO-HUMAN-REVIEW(PR-611). Earlier Codex comments at fb89d18eda17812e3559733ef64b06f14a91c245 are historical and do not approve the rebased head.

## Known Limits

KVM still lacks sync(2), synthetic fdinfo syncfs intentionally returns ENOSYS, and no Hermit pin or parity-manifest cell is included here.
title: Handle KVM syncfs semantics
